metadata.title: Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks as Generative Models

nodes.statement: Let us denote the input to a recurrent neural network by X = leftlbrace x_t rightrbrace where x_t in R^N is an input vector for each time step t.
nodes.raw_latex:
Let us denote the input to a recurrent neural network by $\mathbf{X} = 
\left\lbrace \mathbf{x}_t \right\rbrace$ where $\mathbf{x}_t \in \mathbb{R}^N$ 
is an input vector for each time step $t$.
nodes.clean_text: Let us denote the input to a recurrent neural network by X = leftlbrace x_t rightrbrace where x_t in R^N is an input vector for each time step t.

nodes.statement: Our goal is to model the distribution P left( Y | X right).
nodes.raw_latex:
Our goal is to model 
the distribution $P \left( \mathbf{Y} | \mathbf{X} \right)$.
nodes.clean_text: Our goal is to model the distribution P left( Y | X right).

nodes.statement: The structure of a basic RNN with one hidden layer is illustrated in Figure~, where the output y_t is determined by Pleft(y_t mid \x_d\_d=1^tright) = phi left( W_y h_t + b_y right) where h_t = tanh left( W_h h_t-1 + W_x x_t + b_h right) and W_y, W_h, and W_x are the weight matrices connecting the hidden to output layer, hidden to hidden layer, and input to hidden layer, respectively. b_y and b_h are the output and hidden layer bias vectors, respectively.
nodes.clean_text: The structure of a basic RNN with one hidden layer is illustrated in Figure~, where the output y_t is determined by Pleft(y_t mid \x_d\_d=1^tright) = phi left( W_y h_t + b_y right) where h_t = tanh left( W_h h_t-1 + W_x x_t + b_h right) and W_y, W_h, and W_x are the weight matrices connecting the hidden to output layer, hidden to hidden layer, and input to hidden layer, respectively. b_y and b_h are the output and hidden layer bias vectors, respectively.

define a corruption function that masks $\mathbf{x}_{t}$ as missing,

nodes.clean_text: define a corruption function that masks x_t as missing, and a denoising function that reconstructs it from the others.

nodes.statement: The joint distribution of the time series is defined by first drawing a random permutation o_d of time indices 1dots T and then setting data points observed one by one in that order, starting from a fully missing sequence: P_NADE(Xmid o_d) = prod_d=1^T P(x_o_d mid \x_o_e\_e=1^d-1).
nodes.raw_latex:
The joint 
distribution of the time series is defined by first drawing a random permutation 
$o_d$ of time indices $1\dots T$ and then setting data points observed one 
by one in that order, starting from a fully missing sequence: 
\begin{align}
P_{\mathrm{NADE}}(\mathbf{X}\mid o_d) = \prod_{d=1}^T P(\mathbf{x}_{o_d} \mid \{\mathbf{x}_{o_{e}}\}_{e=1}^{d-1}).
\end{align}
nodes.clean_text: The joint distribution of the time series is defined by first drawing a random permutation o_d of time indices 1dots T and then setting data points observed one by one in that order, starting from a fully missing sequence: P_NADE(Xmid o_d) = prod_d=1^T P(x_o_d mid \x_o_e\_e=1^d-1).

nodes.statement: P_NADE(Xmid o_d) = prod_d=1^T P(x_o_d mid \x_o_e\_e=1^d-1).
nodes.clean_text: P_NADE(Xmid o_d) = prod_d=1^T P(x_o_d mid \x_o_e\_e=1^d-1).

nodes.statement: As the unidirectional RNN models conditional probabilities of the form P_RNN(x_t mid \x_d\_d=1^t-1), we can use Bayes' theorem to derive: hspace2em&hspace-2em P_RNNleft( x_t = a mid \x_d\_dneq t right) \\ & propto P_RNN left( x_t = a mid \x_d\_d=1^t-1 right) P_RNN left(\x_e\_e=t+1^T mid x_t = a, \x_d\_d=1^t-1 right) \\ &= prod_tau=t^T P_RNN(x_tau mid \x_d\_d=1^tau-1) Bigr|_x_t=a where P_RNN(x_tau mid \x_d\_d=1^tau-1) is directly the output of the unidirectional RNN given an input sequence X, where one time step t, i.e. the one we Gibbs sample, is replaced by a proposal a.
nodes.clean_text: As the unidirectional RNN models conditional probabilities of the form P_RNN(x_t mid \x_d\_d=1^t-1), we can use Bayes' theorem to derive: hspace2em&hspace-2em P_RNNleft( x_t = a mid \x_d\_dneq t right) \\ & propto P_RNN left( x_t = a mid \x_d\_d=1^t-1 right) P_RNN left(\x_e\_e=t+1^T mid x_t = a, \x_d\_d=1^t-1 right) \\ &= prod_tau=t^T P_RNN(x_tau mid \x_d\_d=1^tau-1) Bigr|_x_t=a where P_RNN(x_tau mid \x_d\_d=1^tau-1) is directly the output of the unidirectional RNN given an input sequence X, where one time step t, i.e. the one we Gibbs sample, is replaced by a proposal a.

nodes.statement: hspace2em&hspace-2em P_RNNleft( x_t = a mid \x_d\_dneq t right) \\ & propto P_RNN left( x_t = a mid \x_d\_d=1^t-1 right) P_RNN left(\x_e\_e=t+1^T mid x_t = a, \x_d\_d=1^t-1 right) \\ &= prod_tau=t^T P_RNN(x_tau mid \x_d\_d=1^tau-1) Bigr|_x_t=a
nodes.clean_text: hspace2em&hspace-2em P_RNNleft( x_t = a mid \x_d\_dneq t right) \\ & propto P_RNN left( x_t = a mid \x_d\_d=1^t-1 right) P_RNN left(\x_e\_e=t+1^T mid x_t = a, \x_d\_d=1^t-1 right) \\ &= prod_tau=t^T P_RNN(x_tau mid \x_d\_d=1^tau-1) Bigr|_x_t=a
nodes.label: eq:onewayrnn

nodes.statement: As a simple baseline model, we also evaluate the one-gram log-likelihood of the gaps.
nodes.raw_latex:
As a simple baseline model, we also evaluate the \emph{one-gram} log-likelihood 
of the gaps.
nodes.clean_text: As a simple baseline model, we also evaluate the one-gram log-likelihood of the gaps.

nodes.statement: The one-gram model assumes a constant context-independent categorical distribution for the categorical task, or a vector of factorial binomial probabilities for the structured prediction task: P_one-gramleft(y_t right) = f left( b_y right).
nodes.raw_latex:
The one-gram model assumes a constant context-independent 
categorical distribution for the categorical 
task, or a vector of factorial binomial probabilities for the structured 
prediction task:
\begin{equation*}
P_{\mathrm{one-gram}}\left(\mathbf{y}_t \right) = \mathrm{f} \left( \mathbf{b}_y \right).
\end{equation*}
nodes.clean_text: The one-gram model assumes a constant context-independent categorical distribution for the categorical task, or a vector of factorial binomial probabilities for the structured prediction task: P_one-gramleft(y_t right) = f left( b_y right).

nodes.statement: P_one-gramleft(y_t right) = f left( b_y right).
nodes.clean_text: P_one-gramleft(y_t right) = f left( b_y right).

nodes.name: Negative Log Likelihood (NLL) over the test data for the trained models. As a comparison, similar numbers are presented for the unidirectional RNNs trained by citetboulanger2012modeling
nodes.statement: caption Negative Log Likelihood (NLL) over the test data for the trained models. As a comparison, similar numbers are presented for the unidirectional RNNs trained by citetboulanger2012modeling and by citetNIPS2013_5166. The results serve as a sanity check that the trained models have been trained successfully. Note that the BRNN has more context than the unidirectional RNNs, and is hence expected to perform better measured by NLL. Also note that the training of the model for NADE without masking is very similar to the training of the BRNN. textwidth@extracolsepfill l c c c c c hlinenoalign Inference strategy & Wikipedia & Nottingham & Piano & Muse & JSB \\ noalign hline noalign NLL of BRNN & 0.37 & 3.23 & 6.82 & 5.68 & 7.80 \\ NLL of NADE masked & 0.55 & 3.32 & 7.42 & 6.48 & 8.51 \\ NLL of NADE & 0.41 & 2.89 & 7.05 & 5.54 & 7.59 \\ NLL of unidirectional RNN & 1.21 & 3.87 & 7.88 & 7.43 & 8.76 \\ citetboulanger2012modeling & & 4.46 & 8.37 & 8.13 & 8.71 \\ citetNIPS2013_5166 & 1.12 &&&& \\ hline
